newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power extends rise on colder temps.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power extends rise on colder temps.

text.p: Colder thermometer readings Thursday in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool continued to push up day-ahead bulk prices in the Mid-Atlantic electricity market.
"The weather is just going be cold enough to push rates higher," said a PJM trader.
The pool operator declared the grid would continue to operate as a "split system" Thursday due to high power flows into the eastern part of the system, market sources said.
High demand last week in eastern PJM for generation in the west triggered transmission limits in the pool.

A refueling outage at the 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear unit in Pennsylvania further cut power flows eastward, forcing utilities to fire up expensive oil and natural gas plants to balance the grid if they should need to bring cheap, coal-fired power from the west.
Peak, next-hour dispatch rates in the eastern part of the grid remained at $38.70 a megawatt hour (MWh), while rates in the west jumped $8 to $26.00/MWh, market sources said.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Thursday (excluding transmission costs) was traded in a $27.50-31.75/MWh range, up from Tuesday's $26.50-27.00 for delivery today.
PJM power prices for firm, off-peak delivery Thursday rose to $18.00-20.00 from $16.00-18.00 Tuesday.
Next-week PJM deliveries were quoted at $26.75-27.25. PJM power deliveries until end of February held at $26.50-27.00.
March PJM power prices tightened to $23.85-24.05 from $23.80-24.10 Tuesday.
PJM prices for April and May remained at $21.80-21.90, while June PJM power continued to hold at $24.75-25.00.
July/August PJM power widened to $29.70-$29.90 from Tuesday's $29.70-29.75.
PJM third-quarter deliveries stayed at $27.55-27.75, and fourth-quarter PJM prices firmed to $23.85-24.00 from Tuesday's $23.70-23.80.
Firm, peak 1998 PJM deliveries held at $25.75-25.95 after a series of trades between $25.75-25.85 Tuesday.
The Mid-Atlantic is expected to continue to experience near-normal temperatures across the region for the next several days with peak readings around 30 degrees F.
Overcast skies are expected across much of the northern part of the region with chance light snowfall later today.
Forecast of colder weather also boosted swing natural gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate, which climbed 15 cents to the $3.00 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) level.
But NYMEX Henry Hub gas futures were pushed lower midday by technically-driven selling. At 1206 EST, the March Hub contract were down 9.4 cents at $2.130/mmBtu.
